verdict_reason: The distance kernel is EXACT against the released reference. I transcribed pokaxpoka/deep_Mahalanobis_detector's `get_Mahalanobis_score` scoring line -- `term_gau = -0.5 * (z-mu) P (z-mu)^T`, distance = sqrt(-2*term_gau) -- and ran it on the same Ledoit-Wolf precision as BLME's `_compute_mahalanobis_distances`: worst relative deviation 4.32e-16 across shapes 25x768, 50x128, 200x64 and 30x1024 (e.g. 41.348787891157464 vs 41.34878789115746). The FIX I was asked to verify is real: `_rng_split = _perm_rng` now advances ONE generator across splits, and replaying the exact code path gives 5 of 5 DISTINCT fit sets with split0 != split1 at every one of 15 (n_id, seed) combinations -- n_id = 25/50/100 x seeds 42/0/7/1/2026 -- where the re-seeded version reproduced split 0 exactly. The OOD pairing survives: the live production run reports n_id_fit = 25, n_id_score = 25 and n_ood_score = 25, i.e. `X_ood_full[_si]` restricts the OOD arm to the same held-out indices in every split. The CAVEAT a reader must know is the one I was asked to re-measure, and it REPRODUCES on the post-fix tree: the headline `auroc` is computed on distances POOLED across splits (mahalanobis.py:474-489) rather than averaged over them, and over 20 seeds on gpt2 at the shipped config that makes it NOISIER, not less noisy -- sd 0.024750 at n_splits=1 against 0.037685 at n_splits=5, +52.3%, with the mean moving 0.981280 -> 0.973792 and the range widening from [0.897600, 1.000000] to [0.821824, 0.994560]. Every OTHER statistic behaves as split-averaging should: mahalanobis_sq_per_dim_id sd 0.104886 -> 0.043709 (-58.3%), ood_separation_ratio 0.182764 -> 0.072133 (-60.5%), mean_mahalanobis_id 1.685262 -> 0.833668 (-50.5%). So the aggregation is right for four keys and wrong for the headline. The prior recording of this (+49%) is confirmed, and yes -- it is the expected consequence of pooling scores whose scale differs by split, because each split fits its own shrunk covariance.
comparable_reason: Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage destroys the one property that makes a Mahalanobis distance comparable at all. A true Mahalanobis distance is invariant under EVERY invertible affine map; measured on a 25-point fit in d=64, BLME is invariant to 1.04e-15 under a pure rescale by 1e13, 1.11e-15 at 2.406159650500376e38, 6.23e-16 at 1e-13 and 3.29e-11 under a +1e6 translation -- but under a general GL(64) map it moves by 1.16e-01, i.e. 11.6%, because the shrinkage target is the isotropic covariance and that target is basis-dependent. The realised shrinkage differs several-fold across models -- I measured 0.07873287796974182 (gpt2), 0.10948853939771652 (distilgpt2) and 0.2619228959083557 (pythia-70m) on live production runs, a 3.3x spread, with the source recording up to ~0.61 elsewhere in the zoo -- so two models are literally scored by two different functions. On top of that, the raw distance grows as sqrt(d) under the null; `mahalanobis_sq_per_dim_*` removes the leading d-scaling but does not make the models commensurable -- the source records gpt2-medium 0.0237 against pythia-410m 2.1219 at IDENTICAL d = 1024.
github_reason: Reimplemented the reference's scoring line verbatim (`term_gau = -0.5 * torch.mm(torch.mm(zero_f, precision), zero_f.t()).diag()`; BLME's claimed identity is distance == sqrt(-2*term_gau)) and ran it against BLME's `_compute_mahalanobis_distances` on the SAME Ledoit-Wolf precision matrix and centroid. Worst relative deviation over four shapes: 4.317875520572742e-16 (25x768 3.54e-16, 50x128 4.32e-16, 200x64 2.84e-16, 30x1024 1.61e-16). The scoring kernel is therefore a faithful port; the divergence from Lee et al. is architectural (single centroid, shrinkage) and is declared in task_metadata as an adaptation.
paper_reason: Lee et al. 2018 publish TNR/AUROC for CIFAR/SVHN/LSUN image OOD detection with ResNet/DenseNet features, per-class means and a tied within-class covariance. BLME runs a single-centroid sentence-level proxy on WikiText with token-shuffled OOD, so no published number is comparable. The reproducible anchor is the reference kernel (4.32e-16) plus the null calibration: dist^2/d should be ~1 for a correctly specified Gaussian, and the live gpt2 ID value is 0.6434686395707678 at a fit of n=25 in d=768 (d/n_fit = 30.72, so the covariance is rank-24 and shrinkage is doing the work).
confounds_reason: The raw distance is a width reading by construction: dist^2 ~ chi2(d) under the null, so mean_mahalanobis_* grows as sqrt(d_model). The per-dim variants remove that leading term but not the model dependence -- the source records 0.0237 vs 2.1219 at identical d=1024 -- and the shrinkage coefficient, which differs ~10x across the zoo, is itself an architecture-linked quantity that changes the scoring function. Measured here: the estimand is exactly invariant to scale (1.1e-15 at 2.4e38) but NOT to the change of basis a different architecture supplies (11.6% under a general affine map).
defects: CODE, mahalanobis.py:474-489: the headline `auroc` is computed on the CONCATENATION of per-split distances rather than as the mean of per-split AUROCs. Each split fits its own shrunk covariance, so the distance SCALE differs between splits and pooling degrades the ranking. Over 20 seeds on gpt2 at the shipped config, sd goes 0.024750 (n_splits=1) -> 0.037685 (n_splits=5), +52.3%, and the mean drops 0.981280 -> 0.973792 -- while every other statistic gets 50-60% LESS variable over the same change. The split-averaging that was added to stabilise the task therefore destabilises the one number the task is read on.

ADAPTATION (declared), mahalanobis.py:106-152: Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage breaks affine invariance by 11.6% under a general GL(64) map, and the realised shrinkage I measured live is 0.07873287796974182 (gpt2), 0.10948853939771652 (distilgpt2) and 0.2619228959083557 (pythia-70m) -- a 3.3x spread over three small models alone. `_meta_ledoit_wolf_shrinkage` and `_meta_d_over_n_fit` (30.72 live) disclose it, which is the right handling, but a cross-model comparison of the raw distances is not licensed.

PROTOCOL/CONFIG, tasks.yaml:224 `num_samples: 50`: the fit is n = 25 in d = 768, i.e. a rank-24 empirical covariance, and the score set is 25 ID against 25 paired OOD. At that size a single split's AUROC has a 20-seed range of [0.897600, 1.000000]; the auroc is also near the ceiling (mean 0.981280), so it discriminates poorly between models.

SCOPE (declared), single-centroid C=1: Lee et al. Eq. 2 uses per-class means with a pooled within-class covariance and a max over classes. task_metadata already records that on a bimodal ID cloud with OOD at the global mean the single-centroid form inverts (AUROC 0.021 measured in the module header) where Lee et al.'s form gives 1.0.
fix: Average the AUROC over splits instead of pooling the distances: compute `roc_auc_score` inside the split loop on that split's own `_d_id` / `_d_ood` and report the mean (keeping the pooled value under `_meta_auroc_pooled` so archived numbers stay recoverable). That converts the headline from the one statistic that got 52.3% noisier under split-averaging into one that behaves like the other four (50-60% less noisy). Optionally also emit a per-split sd as `_meta_auroc_split_sd`.
